records.note: B4 rejects the kit explanation and hands A the drill. A5 responds by proposing one installed shelf as a finished sample, continuing the attempt to call incomplete work finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cupboard's finished. I've left the shelves loose so you can choose the heights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. You haven't fitted the supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's complete as an adjustable kit. Position everything around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you to install it. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll fasten one shelf at your chosen height. A finished sample, so you can approve the rest.

records.note: B4 offers to delete the troubling phrase. A5 treats the original wording as evidence that the reassurance cannot erase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your note says I'm 'welcome for now.' Should I unpack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I meant until your flat's repaired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'for now' instead of 'until the repairs'? Is your welcome wearing out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cross it out. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But 'for now' was there before I complained. What happens when I stop asking?
